# CSIT6000V (L1) - Advanced AI Computing and Systems Assignment 2: CUDA Programming Submission deadline: To be announced on Canvas

### I. General Notes

1. This assignment counts for 15 points.

2. This is an individual assignment. You may discuss the assignment with others and consult online resources, but the submitted implementation must be your own work. Academic integrity rules of the course apply.

3. Add your name, student ID, and email in comments at the beginning of your source file.

4. Submit your assignment through Canvas before the announced deadline.

5. Use the supplied tests before submission. Evaluation checks correctness and numerical stability; performance and speedup are not graded.

6. Direct assignment-related questions to the course teaching team through Canvas.

### II. Problem Description

This assignment focuses on implementing scaled dot-product attention using CUDA. Given a query matrix Q, a key matrix K, and a value matrix V:

 $$ \mathrm{Q}\colon\mathrm{M}\times\mathrm{d} \quad \mathrm{K}\colon\mathrm{N}\times\mathrm{d} \quad \mathrm{V}\colon\mathrm{N}\times\mathrm{d} $$ 

compute an output matrix $O$ of shape $M \times d$:

 $$ \mathbf{O}=\mathbf{s o f t m a x}(\mathbf{Q K}^{\mathrm{T}}/\sqrt{\mathrm{d}})\mathbf{V} $$ 

The softmax operation is applied independently to each row. Each output row is a weighted sum of the rows of V. All matrices use contiguous, row-major storage and 32-bit floating-point values (FP32).

<div style="text-align: center;">The task includes one attention head and only the forward computation. No causal mask, dropout, backward pass, or multi-head attention is required.</div>

### III. Sequential Algorithm

The CPU reference attention_sequential.cpp is provided for understanding the operation and comparing results. The following pseudocode uses stable softmax:

for i = 0, ..., M-1:
    for j = 0, ..., N-1:
        S[j] = sum_t Q[i,t] * K[j,t] / sqrt(d)
    m = max_j S[j]
    for j = 0, ..., N-1:
        E[j] = exp(S[j] - m)
    z = sum_j E[j]
    for t = 0, ..., d-1:
        O[i,t] = sum_j (E[j] / z) * V[j,t]

## Numerical stability

The direct expression $\exp(S[j]) / \text{sum}_k \exp(S[k])$ can overflow for large positive scores or underflow to zero for an entire row of large negative scores. Subtracting the row maximum before exponentiation preserves the mathematical result while avoiding these failures:

 $$ \begin{array}{r}{\mathbf{m_{i}}=\operatorname*{m a x}_{\mathrm{j}}\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{i j}},\quad\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i j}}=\exp(\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{i j}}-\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{i}})/\sum_{\mathrm{k}}\exp(\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{i k}}-\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{i}})}\end{array} $$ 

A numerically stable implementation is required for 15 points. An implementation that passes all basic tests but fails stability tests receives 10 points. Equivalent stable methods are accepted.

### IV. Your Implementation Task

Complete attention_forward in attention.cu. The declaration is supplied in attention.h:

void attention_forward(
    const float* Q, const float* K, const float* V,
    float* output, int M, int N, int d);

1. Compute the scaled query-key scores on the GPU.

2. Apply softmax independently to each score row on the GPU.

3. Compute the weighted sum of values and write all output elements on the GPU.

4. Release any temporary device memory allocated by your implementation.

All input and output pointers refer to device memory. The supplied runner handles file input, host/device copies, and output printing. Do not change the inputs. Use the default CUDA stream. Multiple kernels and temporary score matrices are allowed; FlashAttention and kernel fusion are not required.

## Input constraints

 $ 1 \leq M, N \leq 512 $;  $ 1 \leq d \leq 64 $. Input values are finite FP32 numbers with absolute value at most 2048. Dimensions need not be multiples of a CUDA block size. Your implementation must handle boundary threads correctly.

## Compiler and library policy

Assessment uses nvcc with -O2 -std=c++14 and a target appropriate to the GPU and compiler. The package has been tested on an NVIDIA RTX 3090 with CUDA Toolkit 11.0 on course TACC; earlier validation also used CUDA 12.8.

Only standard C++ and CUDA runtime/device features are allowed. Do not use cuBLAS, cuDNN, PyTorch, or other third-party compute libraries. The attention computation must execute in CUDA kernels; a CPU-only solution does not receive credit.

## Numerical comparison

For each output element, the checker requires:

 $$ \mathrm{a b s}(\mathrm{a c t u a l~-~\ r e f e r e n c e})\quad<\mathrm{=~1e-4~+~1e-3~*~a b s}(\mathrm{r e f e r e n c e}) $$ 

NaN and infinity are rejected. The checker also validates output dimensions and element counts. Each test has a 30-second timeout to catch hangs; there is no runtime ranking. Infrastructure failures are resolved before grading.

### VI. Compile and Run

### 1. Local or assigned GPU-server testing

Use a Linux CUDA environment with an NVIDIA GPU, compatible driver, CUDA Toolkit, g++, make, Python 3.6 or newer, and Bash. No third-party Python packages are required. In the extracted student-code directory, run:

source env/activate.sh
make test

A complete and stable implementation should end with:

BASIC: 7/7
STABLE: 5/5
SCORE: 15/15
ALL TESTS PASSED

The original skeleton deliberately returns zeros and is expected to fail. It must be completed before it can pass the tests. For individual runs:

make
./attention_cuda dataset/basic_small.txt
make cpu
./attention_seq dataset/basic_small.txt

The build automatically selects a compatible PTX target. On the tested course TACC node with CUDA 11.0, it uses -arch=compute_80. Compile on the assigned GPU node. Follow the teaching team's instructions if an explicit target is needed.

### 2. TACC testing (when enabled for this assignment)

The supplied configuration has been verified on course TACC. It requests one GPU in the tacc partition and uses the CUDA tools on that node. Your course account must already be activated. The SDK creates or reuses an empty cuda-attention-v1 environment.

Configure your own course account once, if it is not already configured:

tcloud config -u <username> -f <private_key_path>
tcloud init

In the directory containing tuxiv.conf, submit a testing job and inspect its result:

tcloud submit
tcloud ps -j JOB_ID
tcloud cat slurm_log/assignment2-sdk-JOB_ID.log

Run these commands on your SDK client, replacing JOB_ID with the returned ID. Submission uploads the directory and invokes sdk-test.sh on the allocated GPU node to compile and run all tests.

Important: Running tcloud submit is only a test. It does not submit your final assignment to Canvas.

### 3. Example input and output

An input file starts with M N d, followed by M rows of Q, N rows of K, and N rows of V. Each matrix row contains d numbers. For example:

Here, Q = [1], K = [1000; 1001; 1002], and V = [0; 1; 2]. Stable softmax uses the shifted scores [-2, -1, 0]. The expected output is approximately:

RESULT 1 1
1.57521038

This example is included as dataset/stable_positive.txt. Output formatting is handled by the supplied runner. Do not print debugging messages to standard output.

Complete and test attention. cu, add your identification comments, and rename the file to student_id.cu (for example, 20991234.cu). Upload this single CUDA source file to Canvas before the deadline announced there.

Do not submit a ZIP archive, executable, output file, testing log, screenshot, or additional source/header files. The supplied interface and runner will be provided during assessment.
